newsitem.title: INDIA: India soymeal prices ease on dull export demand.
newsitem.headline: India soymeal prices ease on dull export demand.

text.p: Dull overseas demand dragged down Indian soymeal prices sharply during the week as sowing for the 1997/98 (Nov-Oct) soybean crop picked up in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, traders said on Tuesday.
They said soymeal for exports were quoted at $255-257 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship) compared with $268-270 last week.

"Soymeal export prices have fallen by about $65 per tonne in the past one month due to lack of export demand," said one oilmeal trader in the central city of Indore, the hub of India's soybean processing industry.
Traders said soybean prices also fell sharply during the week to 10,000 to 10,400 rupees per tonne from 11,500 to 11,800 rupees last week due to poor domestic demand.
They said sowing in 40 percent of the area in the state was over. Rainfall in the Indore region was good but rainfall in other soybean regions was "not very satisfactory."
Soybean arrivals in the central Indian markets were about 700 tonnes per day compared with about 1,500 tonnes at the same time last year, traders said.
Traders said some 700,000 tonnes soybean was currently with farmers and around 50,000 tonnes soybean with traders and processors.
The Soybean Processors Association of India expects the area under soybean cultivation to increase to 5.7 million hectares from five million in 1996/97.
Traders said that farmers received higher prices for their produce in the 1996/97 season which would tempt them to increase the area under the crop for 1997/98.
